question.worked_solution:
We start by creating a matrix whose columns are made up of our vectors, and then we reduce the matrix to row echelon form:

$$
\begin{aligned} & [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 8 & 12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-2){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 8 & 12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{3} & :={R}_{3}+(-1){R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 4 & 8 & 12\end{aligned}] & {R}_{4} & :={R}_{4}+(-4){R}_{2} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & -1 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The pivot columns correspond to basis vectors, while the non-pivot columns correspond to linearly dependent vectors that can be removed. Here, the reduced matrix has $3$ pivot columns (or alternatively, it has exactly $3$ non-zero rows). 

Therefore, 
$\text{dim}(\text{Span}\{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1 \\ 0 \\ 4\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 0 \\ -1 \\ 8\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1 \\ 2 \\ 12\end{aligned}]\})=3.$
